claims.title: Causal nonlinear whole-stage error and adjoint residual influence
claims.theorem: q=(I-A)^(-1)G delta; output_error <= w^T delta + e_out; w=G(I-A)^(-T)|b|
assumptions: fixed exact reference W and U-form target
nonlinear Lipschitz tube contains candidate-exact stage segments
claims.constructive_conclusion: O(s+stage_edges) scalar backward sweep obtains all influence weights; no contraction norm condition on nilpotent A and no dense inverse required
limits: not an existing native witness implementation
projected Hessenberg inverse norms do not satisfy full-space assumption

claims.title: Coefficient-aware non-estimator local truncation certificate
claims.theorem: actual_local_truncation_error <= tau, where tau is the outward upper value of sum_{j=1}^5 d_j h^j + (M_flow6+M_method6)h^6/720; alternatively tau is epsilon_end plus a verified upper bound for the weighted defect integral
assumptions: C6 flow and reference method on full step tube
quadrature remainder enclosed for defect route
claims.constructive_conclusion: Polynomial/Taylor-jet model supplies computable truncation authority without embedded estimator
limits: derivative enclosure native backend not yet supplied
actual stored binary64 coefficients are not presumed to satisfy exact order conditions

claims.title: Global ODE error including metric transport and all accepted residuals
assumptions: verified exact-flow logarithmic norm on enclosing trajectory tubes
TG1 and TG2 hypotheses at every accepted step
claims.constructive_conclusion: If bound <= requested global budget, finite trajectory global error is certified; fixed dissipative metric and tau<=C h^6 imply E<=E0+CT hmax^5+linear_budget+arithmetic_budget
limits: the theorem is not a native trajectory certificate
future adjoint weights must be bounded prospectively for online use

claims.title: Globally weighted optimal residual allocation
claims.theorem: For rho_i(k)<=R_i q_i^k+eta_i, minimize sum p_i log(R_i/r_i) subject to sum a_i r_i<=B; optimum r_i=min(R_i,p_i/(lambda a_i)), p_i=c_i/(-log q_i)
assumptions: fixed influence weights bound actual regime
all setup/certificate/candidate/fallback cost charged for total-work claim
claims.constructive_conclusion: Optimal continuous scheduled-work budget; integer ceiling overhead <= sum c_i; strict total-work saving when exact schedule difference exceeds extra certificate cost
limits: best common threshold of same backend, not strongest solver
scheduled-count comparison does not automatically compare realized early-stop times
GMRES fitted convergence rate is not a contraction witness

claims.title: Positive parametric arithmetic complexity reduction
claims.constructive_conclusion: At fixed b and L>>m log m, Theta(mL) scheduled work becomes O(L+m log m)
limits: fixed eight-stage RODAS itself does not make m asymptotic
this is not a universal ODE complexity lower-bound improvement
bit-cost and future weight availability need separate accounting
